This occupation inspects, diagnoses, adjusts, and repairs wind turbines, with maintenance covering electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic systems, and it is not a general term for all wind energy engineering or management jobs.

Troubleshoot pitch, variable speed, converter systems, and related component faults and diagnose the generator and control system; specific handling follows training, equipment, and the responsibility scope.

Routine maintenance covers turbines, underground transmission, wind farm substations, and fiber optic sensing control equipment; the division of work follows the project, and not everyone is assumed to operate every system.

Tasks include testing electrical components and working with engineers on schedule to measure structural control systems, and equipment and tool requirements do not grant self-taught people the right to test on site.
Tower climbing inspection and maintenance, fiberglass blade inspection and repair, and assembly support may be part of the duties, with formal training and safety conditions checked separately.
Keep tool and spare parts inventory, collect test and research data, and carry out technical training, since accurate records and communication are part of service delivery.
The U.S. survey shows heights, protection, and confined spaces, and BLS also notes evening and weekend standby and remote offshore travel; this is not a uniform Chinese shift arrangement.
O*NETJobZone3 and RCI are U.S. task background; the BLS typical postsecondary non-degree training and long-term OJT do not stand in for Chinese education, certificates, and employer conditions.
The two directions are an editorial split, and on-site diagnosis, testing, and maintenance all require specific training and authorization.

subject.name: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
subject.summary: The wind turbine service technician corresponds to O*NET49-9081.00, inspecting, diagnosing, adjusting, and repairing wind turbines and handling electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic system faults. The tasks include routine maintenance, planned testing, spare parts management, and operating data collection, and may involve heights, small nacelles, and harsh weather. Wind farm engineering design, development, and continuous operations management are separated separately; knowledge and training, the corresponding work certificates, and unit site authorization cannot be replaced by a job title or a paper exercise.
